messages.subject: Re: Error: record date outside camera operation date range:
messages.subject_clean: Error: record date outside camera operation date range:
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
this error means that there is a mismatch between the dates of your camera trap records and the camera trap operation dates. Check if the camera trap setup and retrieval dates are correct. Often it is simply a typo, e.g. wrong year. You can also use the function camOpPlot which is in the vignette to visualise the active camera trapping period and find outliers:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html#camera-operation

Let me know if the problem persists.

messages.subject: Hierarchical subject metadataSpeciesTag not found
messages.body_plain:
Hello camtrapR users and Juergen,

I'm getting to grips with camtrapR for a very large data set and am testing out the metadatatag usage for each species captured on CT. At present I'm testing it out on an image, which has been renamed, copied to a new folder and tagged in DigiKam according to the hierarchical structure of 'Species' > 'Banteng'. Write to sidecard is not selected. When I check the properties of the images in DigiKam I can clearly see the correct tags, and also in R when I run head(rec.db.Banteng) I can see the tags are present in the HierarchicalSubject (i.e. 'Species|Banteng'). When I try and extract the RecordTable for 'Species', all works fine. When I add the addition of metadataSpeciesTag ="Banteng" and extract the RecordTable I get the following error:

DFRCT001 : 1 images
Warning: DFRCT001:   metadataSpeciesTag 'Banteng' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.
Error: something went wrong. I looked through all those 1 folders and now your table is empty. Did you exclude too many species? Or were date/time information not readable?

I've tried retagging with a new structure (according to the Vignette: Extracting Data from Camera Trapping Images), reinstalling and using different images but still with the same error. My folder structure is: D drive > RenamedImages > Station > CameraA > Species > Banteng. I'm sure it's something simple but I've not been able to get pass this issue and now need a fresh pair of eyes on it. I've already looked through the forum to avoid reposting the same problem but have been unable to solve it from those posts. I've attached the CT image I've been using and the script is below. If someone is able to take a look then I really appreciate it.

PG_wd_StationDir <- file.path("D:/RenamedImages")

Banteng_files <- list.files(PG_wd_StationDir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

rec.db.Banteng <- recordTable(inDir  = PG_wd_StationDir,
IDfrom = "metadata",
cameraID = "filename",
camerasIndependent = FALSE,
minDeltaTime = 0,
deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
timeZone ="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
writecsv = TRUE,
outDir = "D:/RenamedImages",
metadataSpeciesTag ="Banteng",
metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical subject metadataSpeciesTag not found
messages.body_plain:
Hi Penny,
you set up the tag structure in digiKam correctly (hierarchical tag structure of 'Species' > 'Banteng').

The problem is in the argument metadataSpeciesTag = "Banteng". Instead of bantang (the species name) you need to set it to:

metadataSpeciesTag ="Species"

The argument metadataSpeciesTag specifies the name of the tag group that contains the species tags, not the species tag you are interested in. Hence it must be "Species", not "Banteng".

If you are only interested in records of banteng, I recommend you simply subset the record table after running the recordTable function.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,
great to hear it works now.

The function imageRename() will only copy images that are not yet present in the output directory containing the renames images. It will not overwrite images that exist in the output directory. In other words, you can rerun imageRename() with new raw data and the function will add on to your specified output directory, but not change the pictures that are present already. So the tags you may have assign to those images will not be affected when you rerun imageRename().

But please be aware that this is only the case if you do not further rename images after applying the function imageRename(). If you do, e.g. by appending the species name, running imageRename() again will copy those images again, and you will end up with 2 versions of the same image with different file names.

I will update the documentation to make this clear.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: using count information
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kevin, Hi Jim,
it should be possible to adapt the code, but at the moment I don't have the time to do so.

But first of all, I have a question. How would you deal with several groups within the same occasion? Say you record a group of 5 individuals and then later a group of 5 individuals again within the same occasion. If these individuals are unmarked and cannot be identified individually, would you count those as 5 or 10? If there is no way to identify groups or individuals, it may or may not be the same group, so we'd have to decide whether to cound 5 or 10 individuals. What do you think would be the best way to handle this?

Here is a possible workaround if groups can be identified and have a known group size:
1. Treat the groups as "individuals", create a detection history for each group.
2. multiply the detection histories with the respective group sizes
3. sum up all detection histories

If group sizes are unknown, you can run step 1 and 3 (and omit step 2) to get a count of groups. But this also requires the groups to be identifiable.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: recordTable ignores pictures
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rahel,
do you or did someone else handle the data on a Mac? And then maybe move to a different OS? These files beginning with "._" are hidden files on Macs.which containing additional information about files and metadata which are supported by the Mac file system but not supported onthe volume's file systems;

In other words, nothing to worry about. I should turn that warning into a note, so this doesn't scare users.

For more info see here:
https://lists.apple.com/archives/applescript-users/2006/Jun/msg00180.html

To answer the other question, no, camtrapR does not require a particular file name to rename properly. Just don't let the files begin with "._". Also, don't manually add double underscores ("__") to files names. imageRename() does that to separate different pieces of information in file names. These double underscores are user by other functions like recordTable to access those information again.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Marius,
thank you for your interest in camtrapR. I am afraid you will need at least a basic understanding of R to use the package and benefit from it. You can easily find many R tutorials on the web.

For camtrapR, the best starting point is the publication and the package vignettes. The package provides sample data and the vignettes walk you through the analyses. The sample data give you an idea how your spreadsheets should look like. Try this in R:
data(camtraps)
data(recordTableSample)

>From what I understand, you already stored the images in the right directory structure. You may want to run the recordTable function to tabulate the camera trap photos next.

What analyses do you wish to do?

Best regards,
Jürgen
